To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the international financial crisis of 1997-98 had a significant effect on the Argentine economy, but the main causes of its weak economic performance have to be sought on the domestic economic policy, (2) the fiscal policy has not been an active stabilizer, (3) discretionary fiscal policy has been a key element in the Argentine economy, (4) the fiscal stance has not been counter-cyclical, (5) the budgetary response to the economic cycle is not strong

(i) international crises partially accounted, though in decreasing terms, for the weak Argentine economic performance; (ii) main causes have to searched in domestic economic policies; (iii) the discretionary seizing of private pension funds and transfers from the IMF were the main sources of government revenues; (iv) public spending was in root of the government's fiscal strain; (v) the overall cyclical tax revenues sensitivity increased but the fiscal balance's response to GDP did no suffice to check cycles; (vi

(i) International financial crises had a negative impact upon Argentina’s economy; (ii) The Argentine government’s response to crises’ effects was not adequate, as it was based on discretionary fiscal policies; (iii) The discretionary fiscal policies implemented in Argentina were not able to stabilize the economy, and even worsened its performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the recent international financial crises upon emerging economies.
the impact that international financial crises have upon fiscal performance of emerging economies.
the impact of the international financial crises upon emerging economies and the performance of discretionary fiscal policies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
discretionary fiscal policy has been ineffective in the Argentine context.
discretionary fiscal policies have not been able to offset the negative effects of international crises upon Argentina, and that the country’s fiscal stance has been too pro-cyclical.
discretionary fiscal policies were not able to prevent the impact of international crises upon Argentina’s economy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the international crisis has had a significant impact on Argentine economy and the fiscal policy has not played a significant role in the stabilization of the economy.
the Argentine fiscal policy was not only passive but also counter-cyclical, which is not consistent with the government’s declared goal of fiscal consolidation.
the international financial crises had a strong impact upon the Argentine economy, which, nevertheless, could have been mitigated by more appropriate economic and fiscal policies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
discretionary fiscal policies in the recent Argentine crisis were not enough to stabilize the business cycle and, in fact, they contributed to the fiscal strain.
the Argentine economy is highly sensitive to international crises.
the government’s fiscal policy was not countercyclical and that the fiscal strain is not cyclical in nature.
